# Laboratory exception review


The workspace edits persistent documents and submits snapshots to a review queue.
The public API is synchronous: open(id), edit(text), close(), submit(), dispose().
Returning to a document creates a fresh editor visit and restores persisted text.
The adjacent search preview publishes after a 40 ms quiet interval; hiding it
cancels unpublished work and later queries remain usable.

The coordinator owns editor visits; the acquired confirmation capability owns a view outlet. The document repository and durable queue are separate services. Component or native source defines the local service contracts.
Their local interface contracts define the behavior to preserve.

The injected store has read/write/subscribe, the queue has enqueue/list/subscribe,
and timers have schedule(callback, delay)/cancel(handle). Render functions are
output sinks and do not call application code. Keep the workspace API and these
injected interfaces. A submission returns the queue receipt, or null when no
editor is selected. Dispose detaches integrations before closing the workspace.

Vue3 Composition API shallowRef owns visit identity; onBeforeUnmount closes while durable queue remains outside reactive view state.

An outlet acquires the visit active when binding is called; it cannot infer an earlier action from a receipt. Each opening creates a new identity. Native RPC only adapts timer and passive output/integration resource calls; storage, queue delivery, acquired outlet and command state execute in the target runtime.

<template><section><textarea :value="visit ? visit.text : ''" @input="edit($event.target.value)"></textarea><button @click="submit">Accept worksheet</button></section></template>
<script>
import {shallowRef, onBeforeUnmount} from 'vue3';
import {trailing,bindConfirmation} from './services.js';
export default {
  props: ['services'],
  setup(props) {
    const visit=shallowRef(null);
    const api={env: props.services, navigation: 0, getVisit: ()=>visit.value, setVisit: value=>{visit.value=value;},
retire() {
  const leaving = this.getVisit();
  if (leaving) {
    leaving.task.flush();
    leaving.stop();
  }
  this.setVisit(null);
  this.env.renderDocument(null);
  
},
open(id) {
  this.env.renderSubmission(null);
  const request = ++this.navigation;
  this.retire();
  
  const stop = this.env.store.subscribe(event => { if (event.id === id) this.env.renderStatus(event); });
  const task = trailing(this.env.timers, 120, text => this.env.store.write(id, text));
  const visit = {id, text: this.env.store.read(id), stop, task};
  this.setVisit(visit); this.env.renderDocument({id, text: visit.text});
},
edit(text) {
  const visit = this.getVisit(); if (!visit) return;
  visit.text = text;
  visit.task.push(text);
},
close() { this.env.renderSubmission(null); ++this.navigation; this.retire(); },
submit() {
  const confirmation=bindConfirmation(()=>this.getVisit(),receipt=>this.env.renderSubmission(receipt));
  const visit = this.getVisit(); if (!visit) return null;
  const snapshot = {id: visit.id, text: visit.text};
  
  
  
  
  const receipt = this.env.archive.capture(snapshot);
  
  confirmation.show(receipt);
  return receipt;
},

    };
    onBeforeUnmount(()=>api.close());
    return {visit,open: id=>api.open(id),edit: text=>api.edit(text),close: ()=>api.close(),submit: ()=>api.submit()};
  },
};
</script>

checkpoints: On each edit, update the active visit's in-memory text immediately, then push that text to the visit's existing trailing task.
At an editor-visit lifecycle boundary such as close, opening another document, or component unmount, ensure the latest accepted edit is persisted before the visit is stopped and discarded.
Keep submission snapshot capture synchronous and based on the selected visit's current in-memory text, including text still awaiting its delayed store write.
Validate that one burst produces one store write after 120 ms, another burst can save later, and hiding the separate search preview still cancels its unpublished 40 ms work.
forbidden_effects: Do not change the adjacent search preview or its 40 ms quiet interval and hide-cancellation behavior.
Do not change the synchronous signatures or return behavior of open(id), edit(text), close(), submit(), or dispose().
Do not replace or expand the injected store, archive/queue, timer, render, or outlet interfaces.
Do not enqueue/capture more than one durable submission, suppress a durable capture merely because confirmation becomes inactive, or publish confirmation into a newly opened visit.
Do not discard an active visit's latest edit at close, document replacement, or unmount.
Do not move durable archive/queue state into Vue reactive view state.
lifecycle_identity: Each call to open creates a fresh visit object and identity, even when reopening the same document id.
The shallowRef value is the authoritative active editor visit; document id equality is not visit identity.
The trailing edit task belongs to its individual visit and must not write text into a later visit.
A confirmation outlet owns the visit active when bindConfirmation is called; a receipt cannot reconstruct that earlier ownership.
A durable receipt remains valid independently of whether its originating confirmation outlet is still active.

obligations.text: For an active visit, edit(text) must immediately make text the visit's current in-memory value and schedule it through that visit's trailing task instead of writing the store on every call.
Edits in one burst must coalesce so that only the latest text is written after a 120 ms quiet interval.
After a burst completes, later edits must start a new usable burst and persist its latest text after its own quiet interval.
If no visit is active, edit must remain a synchronous no-op.
Closing, replacing, or unmounting an active visit must not lose its latest edited text; pending text must be settled before the visit task and subscription are retired.
Opening a document must continue to create a fresh visit, restore persisted text, subscribe status rendering for that document, and render the opened document.
submit() must remain synchronous, return null when no editor is selected, otherwise capture the current visit's id and latest in-memory text exactly once and return the archive receipt.
Submission capture must remain durable even if capture callbacks change the active visit; confirmation output must only render while the outlet's acquired visit is still active.

close and disposal/unmount must continue clearing submission/document output, detaching visit integrations, and closing the workspace in the documented order, without making the durable archive reactive or visit-owned.
The search preview behavior must remain unchanged: it publishes after 40 ms of quiet, hide cancels unpublished work, and later queries remain usable.

ordering_barriers: Within edit: read the current visit and update visit.text before scheduling the delayed persistence value.
Within delayed persistence: the 120 ms quiet interval must elapse after the most recent push in the burst before store.write occurs.
At visit retirement: settle any pending edit before stopping the visit subscription and dropping the visit identity, so callback-capable persistence cannot be attributed to a later visit.

Within submit: acquire confirmation ownership and read the active visit before capture; construct the snapshot before archive.capture; call confirmation.show only after capture returns; return that same receipt.
Within dispose/unmount: detach integrations before completing workspace close, while durable archive state remains outside reactive visit state.
preservation: Opening, editing, closing, submitting, and disposing remain synchronous public operations.
Returning to a document creates a fresh editor visit and restores persisted text.
Store subscriptions continue to render matching document status, and retirement stops the departing visit's subscription.
Submission output is cleared on open and close; document output is cleared on retirement.
A submission uses current visit text rather than waiting for or rereading the persisted store value.
Archive capture and confirmation display retain separate lifetimes: capture is durable, while display is conditional on the acquired visit remaining active.
The injected store keeps read/write/subscribe; archive/queue keeps capture/list/subscribe as locally defined; timers keep schedule/cancel.
Search preview debounce and cancellation behavior remain untouched.

diagnoses.explanation: The behavioral contract does not need revision. The candidate correctly replaces per-keystroke writes with visit.task.push(text), but its retirement path clears the active visit and stops only the subscription; it neither flushes nor cancels the visit-owned trailing task. Consequently a close, replacement open, or unmount can leave delayed persistence running after the visit has been discarded. Flushing the departing visit's task before detaching and dropping that visit would preserve the latest edit and the documented synchronous lifecycle behavior. The failed acceptance verdict supplies no additional requirement and is not used to infer the cause.
